items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-01-16
items.q: I never did know that boy's real name... They called him Jelly Roll Morton, that's all I know about him. He's a good ragtime piano player... I used to meet him, going to wake, and sometimes we'd go over together on the boat in the morning.

ctx.x: Was that his name at that time, Charlie?

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-01-16
items.q: You said you knew him too, huh? ... I don't know him this piano school. He used to be here a while back on Bayeson Street.

ctx.x: What about Jelly Roll Morton? You said you knew him too, huh?

Jelly Roll? Uh-huh. I don't know him this piano school. He used to be here a while back on Bayeson Street. And he left here. He went around Monroe, went home, and from there he'd come back here again. He played piano all over around Vichy Corral, mostly on Basin Street, mostly. Who would he be working for? And in 1917, he went back home again in 1917, he came to Chicago. And he'd be around at 35th and State at the E-light Cabaret. Used to visit there, you know.
